historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle volume path (copper 741kt FY2025 -> ~1Mt by 2028 group capacity, gold ramping to 20t/yr by ~2030) at normalised prices. The equity 5y CAGR of 16.2% and EPS 5y CAGR of 53.9% are measured from the FY2020 cycle trough (cobalt near 9-year lows, pre-KFM) to the FY2025 cobalt-quota peak and are not a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (16.2%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (12.8%) and from EPS CAGR (53.9%); owner-FCF CAGRs (45.8% / 130.5%) are off a near-zero FY2020 base (RMB179m). All are cycle artefacts; forward growth is set from volumes and mid-cycle prices, not from any of them.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (no SBC, interest income left in because the company is net-debt). FY2020 owner FCF RMB871m, FY2022 RMB4,936m, FY2025 RMB13,260m; FY2024 was RMB27,485m on a working-capital release that reversed in FY2025 (OCF 32.4bn -> 20.8bn while profit rose 50%).

scenario_narratives.base: Peak-cycle FY2026 banked (H1 already reported +86% net profit), then mid-cycle: copper ~US$9,000/t, cobalt ~US$25k/t as DRC quotas evolve into a managed-but-looser regime, copper volume to ~1Mt by 2028 and gold to ~10t by 2030. Absolute EBITDA dips from ~RMB58bn (FY2026) to ~RMB45bn (FY2028) and grows with volume thereafter; capex peaks at RMB14bn through the build-out, then 4% of revenue. The axes that matter are (1) where cobalt settles once the export quota is no longer the price-setter, (2) whether DRC fiscal terms hold, and (3) copper price versus the volume ramp.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper >US$10,500/t sustained, cobalt kept at ~US$40k/t by a durable DRC quota, 1Mt copper by 2028, 20t gold by 2030, lower NCI leakage; 21% margin in perpetuity (~RMB65bn EBITDA by FY2030).
scenario_narratives.bear: Cobalt rally unwinds to US$15-20k/t, copper US$7,500/t, DRC fiscal re-negotiation lifts leakage to 43%, gold build-out overruns; 12.5% margin from FY2028 (~RMB30bn EBITDA).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value CMOC as a volume-growing, mid-cycle copper-cobalt producer, not at today's cobalt-quota earnings. The owner's question is what ~1Mt of low-cost copper plus by-product cobalt, Mo/W, Nb/P and a nascent gold business earns through a cycle, after the DRC's take (tax, royalty, Gecamines) and minority partners, discounted at a CNY cost of capital with the DRC risk carried in a heavy bear weight rather than in the discount rate. Debt-like prepayments (stream, CATL) and the Gecamines settlement are deducted because the revenue they pre-paid is in the projections.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cobalt price: the 2025-26 rally is a DRC export-policy artefact; base assumes US$25k/t mid-cycle, bear US$15-20k/t -- every US$10k/t on ~60-100kt of sellable cobalt is ~RMB4-7bn of EBITDA
DRC fiscal and regulatory terms: quota administration, royalty renegotiation, Gecamines minimum dividends; modelled as 40-43% combined leakage
Copper price versus the 1Mt volume ramp: base US$9,000/t; FY2026 run-rate embeds >US$10k/t
Capex intensity of TFM III / KFM II / Cangrejos and gold-acquisition integration; FY2025 OCF fell 36% on working capital while profit rose 50%
A/H and CNY/HKD basis: IV is computed in CNY and converted at 1.1751; the H-share trades at a 28.5% discount to the A-share, so an A/H re-rating is upside not modelled
IXM trading revenue (~70% of consolidated) makes %-of-revenue drivers small and sensitive to trading volumes; the absolute EBITDA/capex paths are the real assumptions

inputs.share_count_basis: 17,460,842,176 A + 3,933,468,000 H shares = 21,394.3m at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report). Held FLAT: SBC is immaterial (expensed at 0%), treasury shares are RMB18m, the USD1.2bn zero-coupon H-share convertible (conversion price HK$28.03 vs HK$13.01 spot) is deep out of the money and carried as DEBT, not as dilution; the H-share restricted share scheme mandate (up to 393m H shares, 1.8%) has no material grants yet.
inputs.debt_composition: 30 June 2026, RMB m: short-term borrowings 35,861 + long-term borrowings 598 + non-current liabilities due within one year 2,515 + non-current lease liabilities 105 = 39,079 (the DB total_debt), PLUS the USD1.2bn zero-coupon H-share convertible bonds due 2027 issued 26 Jan 2026, booked inside 'other current liabilities' (9,378 vs 969 at FY2025 => ~8,408 liability component; cash receipt 8,221). Total 47,487. EXCLUDED: 'held-for-trading financing liabilities' 9,161 (IXM trading-book repo/financing, matched by held-for-trading financial assets and trading inventory inside working capital). Cash is the cash-flow-statement closing balance 39,485 (unrestricted); balance-sheet cash and bank balances 42,523 include ~3.0bn restricted.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR note (XII) Share-based payments: the only plan is the 2021 Phase I ESOP (48.5m A shares at RMB2, fully vested), cumulative equity-settled charge RMB133.8m since 2021; cash-settled share-based payments RMB1.0m in FY2024 and nil in FY2025. Immaterial against RMB45bn EBITDA -- treated as zero (SBC-zero market, house = street).
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2025 or H1 FY2026 (phase III buyback was FY2022). Flat count is a modelling convention the company is not paying for, but SBC is ~0 so there is nothing to fund.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. fx_rate = 1.1751 HKD per CNY (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-23; inverse HKDCNY=X 0.8501). Direction: model(CNY) -> quote(HKD), i.e. IV_HKD = IV_CNY x 1.1751. Parity check: the A-share 603993.SS closed CNY14.23 = HK$16.72 at this rate against the H-share HK$13.01, an A/H premium of 28.5% -- a normal A/H dual-listing spread, not an FX error (the H discount is structural, so the check confirms direction and magnitude, not a tie). sanity_check.py is known to read fx_rate in the opposite direction on CNY/HKD tickers (memory: systemic fx-direction bug); multiples it prints for this ticker should be re-read with that in mind.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y CGB risk-free ~1.8%, China/EM equity risk premium 6.5%, beta 1.25 for a DRC-concentrated copper-cobalt producer => cost of equity 9.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (RMB bank lines + zero-coupon USD CB), 25% tax => 2.6% after tax; D/(D+E) 12% at the HK$278bn market cap => WACC 0.88x9.9 + 0.12x2.6 = 9.0%. No DRC/cobalt-policy premium is stacked on top: that risk is charged once, in the bear scenario's flows and its 30% weight. Same 9.0% in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS-16-style lease liabilities (non-current 105 + current portion inside non-current liabilities due within one year) sit in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; lease-asset renewal (right-of-use assets RMB241m) is immaterial and is inside the capex % line. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: minority shareholders (Gecamines 20% of TFM, CATL/others 28.75% of KFM, Brazil partners) are folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-plus-leakage rate so the projected NOPAT is attributable-only. Calibration: FY2025 attributable net income 20,339 / (EBIT ex net finance 35,161) = 57.8% => 42% leakage (ETR 31.7% + NCI 14% of post-tax); H1 FY2026 16,152 / 25,705 = 62.8% => 37% (NCI share fell to 9.7% as cobalt/Chinese-segment profits rose). Base uses 40%. The NCI book value (RMB18,990m) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon, cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf-adaptations.md: CNY-built WACC, CNY->HKD bridge, leases as debt, NCI folded into leakage, excluded-income assets added back, SBC-zero, risk charged once). Routed as 'operating company, non-US, cyclical' -- a commodity producer with a metals-trading arm; not a holdco or financial. Fresh build, no prior DCF. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION is the central judgment: FY2025 (EBITDA ~RMB45bn, 21.8% margin) and H1 FY2026 (annualising ~RMB60bn, ~22.8%) are peak-cycle -- cobalt above US$50k/t is a DRC export-quota artefact, copper above US$10k/t is at the top of its range. The base path banks FY2026 near the run-rate (H1 already reported), then glides the EBITDA margin to a 17.5% mid-cycle level by FY2028 (copper ~US$9,000/t, cobalt ~US$25k/t, Mo/W/Nb/P flat, gold ramping to ~10t), which on ~RMB260bn of revenue is ~RMB45bn of EBITDA -- i.e. FY2025's absolute EBITDA re-earned on 25-30% more copper volume at normal prices. Consolidated revenue is ~70% low-margin IXM trading pass-through, so every %-of-revenue driver is small and the margin paths are what carry the judgment; the absolute EBITDA, capex and NOPAT paths are the checks. Interest income (RMB1,644m FY2025) is NOT deducted from last_fcf: the company is net-debt (RMB8bn financial, RMB26.7bn with debt-like items), and the component build is unlevered -- EBITDA excludes interest income and expense, both land in the net-debt bridge. Engine basis: the engine builds from base_revenue x paths; last_fcf is an audit anchor. Debt-like obligations that are NOT financial debt but reduce future cash on revenue the model projects are deducted in equity_bridge (metal-stream prepayment, CATL offtake prepayment, Gecamines settlement); equity-accounted and other non-current financial assets, whose income is outside EBITDA, are added at book (matching-asset rule).

bear.narrative: The cobalt rally unwinds: quota enforcement loosens or ARECOMS releases the strategic reserve, LFP/high-nickel substitution bites, cobalt returns to US$15-20k/t; copper mean-reverts to US$7,500/t on a China/global slowdown; the DRC re-opens fiscal terms (a second Gecamines-style settlement, higher royalties) lifting leakage to 43%; Cangrejos permitting slips and capex overruns while volumes still grow. EBITDA margin 12.5% from FY2028 (~RMB30bn), between FY2023's 10.9% and FY2024's 16.6%.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +25%: H1 FY2026 revenue +42.8% (RMB135.3bn) on cobalt sales catch-up, copper volume +9.7% and IXM volumes; H2 assumed ~RMB123bn (vs RMB111.9bn H2 FY2025) => ~RMB258bn. FY2027 -3% as cobalt realisations normalise and IXM pass-through falls with prices, offset by copper +8%. FY2028-30 +5/+5/+4% from KFM Phase II and TFM Phase III toward 1Mt copper and the first Brazilian/Ecuador gold volumes; then 3% to 2.5%.
base.margin_note: 22.5% FY2026 (H1 FY2026 annualises ~22.8%: PBT 25.7bn + net finance 0.6bn + D&A ~4.0bn on 135.3bn); 19.5% FY2027 as cobalt falls from >US$50k/t toward US$30k/t; 17.5% from FY2028 = mid-cycle (copper US$9,000/t, cobalt US$25k/t) -- ~RMB45bn absolute EBITDA, i.e. FY2025's level re-earned on 25-30% more copper at normal prices. FY2024 (16.6%) and FY2023 (10.9%) bracket the downside at smaller volumes.
base.capex_note: FY2025 cash capex RMB7.6bn (3.7%), H1 FY2026 RMB4.9bn plus RMB5.9bn of gold-mine acquisitions. TFM Phase III + KFM Phase II + Cangrejos (PFS capex ~US$925m) + Brazilian gold + sustaining => ~RMB13-15bn/yr FY2026-28 (5.0-5.5%), easing to 4% (~RMB11-12bn sustaining + replacement) once the 1Mt platform is built.
base.tax_note: 40% combined cash tax + NCI leakage (see inputs.nci_treatment): ETR ~31.7% FY2025 (DRC 30% + China 15-25% + Brazil) and NCI ~12% of post-tax profit.
base.wc_note: Negative capture: receivables + trading inventories (RMB45bn + long-term inventories) far exceed payables; IXM's working capital is funded by the short-term borrowings already in net debt, so growth consumes cash and the FY2027 revenue dip releases it.

bull.narrative: Copper holds above US$10,500/t on electrification/AI-power demand and concentrate scarcity; the DRC quota regime persists through 2027 and is replaced by a managed system that keeps cobalt around US$40k/t; CMOC reaches 1Mt copper by 2028 and 20t gold by 2030; NCI leakage is lower (38%) as the Chinese and Brazilian segments grow. EBITDA margin settles at 21%, ~RMB65bn by FY2030.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: profit is concentrated in one jurisdiction with one discretionary regulator (ARECOMS quotas, Gecamines fiscal history), and the current earnings peak rests on a policy-made cobalt price rather than demand. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to hold at once -- copper above US$10.5k, a durable cobalt quota, and a new gold business delivering on time in Ecuador/Brazil. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
